pr_title: Truncate long usernames in private chat tab
pr_comments:
I think you want to use `MaxWidth`.

Also should probably remove the "bold" version and just combine them.

Also should probably be done at the base class, not just `PrivateChannelTab`.

Sorry, only just getting used to the framework.

> I think you want to use `MaxWidth`.

I couldn't find a `MaxWidth` property. Does this need be implemented at SpriteText-level in framework?


> Also should probably remove the "bold" version and just combine them.

Looking into this, the two versions are probably there to [fade seamlessly](https://github.com/ppy/osu/blob/master/osu.Game/Overlays/Chat/Tabs/ChannelTabItem.cs#L206) 
from Medium to Bold font weight. Not sure how to combine them and still retain the animation.


> Also should probably be done at the base class, not just `PrivateChannelTab`.

I included "czechoslovak" in the screenshot too as the longest name for a non-private channel and it has plenty of space. I could give the base class a longer maximum for future added channels though.

Thanks for your patience.
I think it's fine to remove the fade animation for now. And sorry, width is actually correctly - I was thinking of a different class.

The reasoning for moving to the base class is because if there *was* a channel which was too long, it should be truncated. It's guarding against future failure.

Also it means you can specify the width and truncation mode in the object initialisers, which should feel much cleaner.

Adressed your points. Although it's not much cleaner as
- you still have to specify a different `Width` for the derived class.
- In  `ChannelSelectorTabItem`  
  ```
    Text.Font     = Text.Font.With(size: 45);
    TextBold.Font = Text.Font.With(size: 45); 
  ```
  made sure that `ChannelSelectorTabItem` wasn't bold when active.
  I replaced this with a virtual `IsBoldWhenActive` and it feels kinda wonky

I think you can fix up the size specs by making the text `RelativeSizeAxes = Axes.X` and applying a padding to avoid it overlapping the close button. Then you should not need to specify the different width values.

Would still need to override that behaviour for the `+`-Button though,
so it's only more of a headache from there :/
Why do you need to override?

Perhaps I misunderstood?
I can't think of any way to add a fixed padding that doesn't break the `+`-button

- right padding on enclosing container 
- left padding/margin on the `CloseButton`
- right padding/margin on the `OsuSpriteText`

I was thinking something like this in the base class (confirmed to work)

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/191335/62006475-d0948980-b17b-11e9-8cbf-ff13d537347a.png)

truncation would need to still be disabled on the selector tab, though.

@peppy I'm still missing something, aren't I 
![oops](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/46070579/62006762-55b07c00-b145-11e9-9d02-b02df848149a.PNG)
Hmm, I see. Do you have a test scene for this? I can take a further look.
Ah, nevermind, it's Padding instead of Margin 👍

No, that still didn't do it.
I don't have a test scene as I thought this would be a one liner.
Sorry for stalling, could you take over please? 
I'm kinda in over my head on this one.
I've made the required changes. Please have a look and see what you think.
Thanks, I like this solution. Should be good.
@smoogipoo requesting review since I made considerable changes.
